title: Reducing highest-priority critically important antimicrobial prescribing in four small-animal clinics: a quality improvement project
abstract: Problem: in a group of four small-animal clinics, 27 percent of systemic antimicrobial prescriptions for dogs and cats were highest-priority critically important antimicrobials, against a guideline that reserves them for cultured cases. Intervention: a prescribing prompt, a consult-room guide, time-limited free urine culture, owner tablet-giving support and monthly clinic feedback, tested in four PDSA cycles. Measures: weekly HPCIA share on a run chart, with amoxicillin-clavulanate share, 7-day re-consultation and owner complaints as balancing measures. Results and conclusions will be written after 16 intervention weeks.
introduction: HPCIAs are prescribed in companion animal practice more often than guidelines advise, often without culture and often as long-acting injections for cats. Prompts and feedback have been followed by lower use in single-practice and small controlled reports, but substitution and clinical outcomes are rarely measured.
methods: Model for Improvement with four PDSA cycles from October 2026 to January 2027 after a 12-week retrospective baseline. The weekly HPCIA share comes from the practice management system report builder using a fixed product list; run chart rules were fixed before the baseline was extracted. Culture before treatment is sampled by hand monthly. The project was classified as quality improvement by the group's clinical governance committee.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the annotated weekly run chart, the p-chart, the balancing and process measure charts, and prompt reasons by cycle.
discussion: The discussion will interpret any shift against the run chart rules and recorded co-interventions, compare its size with the retrieved prompt and feedback reports, examine substitution, and state what the group will keep after free culture ends.
limitations: Four clinics in one group; no concurrent comparison; an outcome measure of prescribing rather than animal health; indication-specific measures rest on monthly samples.
conclusion: To be written after the final cycle; it will be limited to prescribing in these clinics and will not claim effects on resistance or animal outcomes.
summary: SQUIRE-structured draft with results left empty until data exist.
